subject: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation plan & benchmarks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Su <daniel.su@healthgrid.com>, Priya Rao <priya@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation plan & benchmarks

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) milestone focused on the technical evaluation/benchmarking phase so we can validate performance and cost before finalizing procurement. I attached a short MAP draft (HealthGrid_MAP_TechEval_v1.docx) and a lightweight bench harness (bench-harness-v1.zip).

High-level proposed milestone: Technical evaluation (two-week sprint)
- Objective: Verify model shortlist against HealthGrid production-like prompts and traffic pattern; validate latency, cost, and output quality to inform final model selection.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - End-to-end P95 latency (inference path) <= 200 ms for 512-token responses (target environment: Dedicated pool or Private deployment; we will measure on both hosted API and private config)
  - Token-level cost goal: <= $0.02 per 1k output tokens for the recommended configuration (batching + quantization)
  - Quality: >= 92% pass-rate on core prompt set (see attached benchmark-results-template.xlsx)
- Model shortlist for evaluation: Llama 2 70B (int8/q4), Mistral Large 7B (optimized), Falcon 40B Instruct (quantized variant) — we can expand if you prefer other candidates.

Proposed responsibilities / timeline:
- HealthGrid: provide representative prompt set (sample ~1500 prompts) and a test account/VM for private runs if needed — due: 2026-03-05
- Redwood (Neha & Vivek): run initial hosted benchmarks, provide recommended configs (batching, kv-cache settings, quantization profile) and a short report — due: 2026-03-12
- Joint: 1-hour benchmark kickoff to align on dataset and measurement scripts (propose 2026-03-03 or 2026-03-04)

Dependencies / notes:
- Procurement / security sign-off may be needed for Private deployment (procurement@healthgrid.com). Please confirm if HealthGrid requires a VPC/on-prem deployment for this evaluation or if hosted API is acceptable for initial runs.
- We plan to measure both p50/p95 latencies, throughput (req/s) under 50 concurrent connections, and unit cost using our Optimize toolkit.

Next steps:
1) Confirm dataset handoff and permission model (who will share the prompts).
2) Pick a kickoff time for the benchmark run.
3) Confirm that procurement is looped in for any access needs.

If that looks reasonable I’ll update the MAP doc and lock dates.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: HealthGrid_MAP_TechEval_v1.docx, bench-harness-v1.zip
From: Daniel Su <daniel.su@healthgrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@healthgrid.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation plan & benchmarks

Thanks Marissa — appreciated summary. We had a good internal sync after the call. A few quick items from our side: 

- Availability: 2026-03-04 10:00am PT works for a kickoff.
- Dataset: Priya will put together an anonymized prompt dump (~1500 prompts) and share via a secure S3 link by 2026-03-05. We will include some longer-context examples (up to 1k tokens) to test KV-cache performance.
- Procurement: looping procurement@healthgrid.com for any contractual/procurement flow — they won’t need to see technical detail yet but will need the final pricing cadence.

A couple of constraints we need to make explicit in the MAP: 
- Target E2E P95 under load should be <= 180–200 ms for 512-token responses; anything above ~250 ms will be a hard blocker for our UI.
- Unit-cost threshold we’d like to hit is <= $0.02 per 1k output tokens; if the hosted option materially exceeds that we’ll need to test Dedicated/Private configs for cost parity.
- Data residency: HealthGrid requires EU residency for PHI workflows, but this initial eval is US-based and anonymized — we still need a note in the MAP about production residency options.

Questions for Redwood team:
- Can you confirm whether the bench-harness will report p95 latency excluding network transfer to client (i.e., server-side inference only)?
- Do you support running the same harness in a VPC-connected private deployment we will provision?

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Daniel
Daniel Su
VP of Engineering | HealthGrid Inc
daniel.su@healthgrid.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Su <daniel.su@healthgrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation plan & benchmarks

Hi all — quick technical clarifications and updated run plan based on Daniel’s notes.

1) Bench harness metrics: the harness we supplied will report both server-side inference latency (model-only, excluding client network) and end-to-end latency when run from a client VM. We’ll provide a breakdown: model forward time, batching overhead, and network RTT.

2) VPC/private run: yes — we can run the same harness inside a VPC/private deployment. For that we’ll need a small VM (Docker-friendly) from HealthGrid to run the client driver and a service account/key with access to your test bucket. We’ll describe the minimal network firewall rules in the MAP.

3) Updated benchmark plan (short):
- Phase A (Hosted): Redwood runs hosted API benchmarks across the shortlist (Llama 2 70B q4, Mistral 7B opt, Falcon 40B q4) with three configs: (a) baseline, (b) batching enabled (burst 8), (c) quantized model + batching. Deliverable: host_bench_report.pdf — due 2026-03-10.
- Phase B (Private/VPC): run same harness inside HealthGrid VPC to measure delta and validate residency constraints. Deliverable: private_bench_report.pdf — due 2026-03-12.

4) Bench success gating (we’ll use these to recommend final model):
- Latency: server-side p95 <= 200 ms for 512-token generative responses (preferred <= 180 ms).
- Throughput: sustain >= 25 requests/sec for 512-token responses with <= 2x p95 increase vs baseline.
- Quality: at least 92% pass-rate on core prompt set per HealthGrid scoring rubrics.
- Cost: throughput-weighted token cost <= $0.02 per 1k output tokens across preferred config.

5) Responsibilities (confirmed):
- HealthGrid: share anonymized prompt set + scoring rubric; provision small client VM for private run; confirm procurement contact — due 2026-03-05 (Priya).
- Redwood: run hosted benchmarks + private run; provide config recommendations + delta analysis — deliverables due 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-12 (Neha/Vivek).

I’ve attached bench-harness-v1.zip (scripts + CI snippets) and the benchmark-results-template.xlsx. If the deadlines above look tight, we can shift the private run by a couple days.

Neha Kapoor
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference

Thanks everyone — nice alignment. I updated the MAP doc (HealthGrid_MAP_TechEval_v1.docx) to reflect the responsibilities, deliverables, and dates we discussed. Key updated items:

- Kickoff: 2026-03-04 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).
- HealthGrid deliverables: anonymized prompt set + scoring rubric (due 2026-03-05).
- Redwood deliverables: hosted bench report (due 2026-03-10), private run report (due 2026-03-12), final recommendation and cost model by 2026-03-15.
- MAP milestone target close date (commercial): 2026-03-25 — dependent on bench results and procurement timeline.

Action items (please reply to confirm):
1) @Priya — confirm S3 share + whether you can provision the small client VM for the private run by 2026-03-05.
2) @procurement@healthgrid.com — is there any paperwork we should prepare in parallel to avoid delays if benchmarks are green? (standard SOW + PO cadence would be helpful).
3) @Neha / @Vivek — confirm you’ll run Phase A on 2026-03-06 and share data format requirements for the prompt set.
